Name: Jabberwocky
Description: Full-featured integrated toolhead for Voron 2.4 and Trident. Includes filament cutter, dual filament sensors, nozzle LEDs, NitéHawk 36 toolboard, and BMG-derived drive gears. Designed for multi-material compatibility with MMU-style systems. Ships as non-assembled kit with LDO NEMA14 motor and Phaetus Conch hotend.
Pros: Built-in filament cutter; dual filament sensors; NitéHawk 36 CAN toolboard included; LEDs (nozzle + status); multi-material ready out of box; strong community support
Cons: Higher cost than DIY options; Conch hotend limits future hotend swaps; NEMA14 motor may require retuning

Name: Mailbox
Description: A Voron V0.1 and V0.2 toolhead that uses the guts of a 5015 fan for part cooling and incorporates Neopixel RGBW LEDs. Compatible with the Mini-AfterSherpa mounting pattern and works on Voron Trident, V2.4, Switchwire, and Legacy via adapter mounts.
Included Hotend: Hotend-agnostic (mounts available for most common hotends)
Included Extruder: LGX Lite, Orbiter v1.5, Voron PocketWatch 2, RoundHouse, RoundAbout, RoundTrip
Pros:
Unique 5015 fan gutted for high-volume part cooling
Neopixel RGBW LED integration
No X or Z travel loss on V0.2
Works with Mini-AfterSherpa extruder mounting pattern
Mounts available for Trident, V2.4, Switchwire, and Legacy
Cons:
5015 fan modification requires careful disassembly
May tap door/tophat on V0.1
Less cooling symmetry than dual 4010 designs

Name: Peregrine
Description: Commercial toolhead from Excit3D, designed for high-speed CoreXY printing. Sold as a kit or assembled unit. Targeted at Voron 2.4 and RatRig V-Core users seeking a commercial-grade toolhead upgrade with reduced mass.
Pros: Commercial quality; reduced mass for high-acceleration printing; active vendor support from Excit3D
Cons: Price and availability depend on Excit3D stock; smaller community than Voron Design toolheads; specs need verification from vendor page (JS-rendered, not fetchable)

Name: Rainbow Dragon
Description: A Voron and Printers for Ants toolhead specifically designed for the Phaetus TaiChi dual filament hotend. Enables dual-filament printing on V0-class and Printers for Ants machines.
Pros:
Native dual-filament support on small-format printers
Designed by chirpy2605 with extensive community testing
Prints-for-ants compatible
Cons:
Requires Phaetus TaiChi hotend — not hotend-agnostic
Dual filament adds complexity to wiring and tuning

Name: Archetype
Description: Modular community toolhead system for Voron 2.4 and Trident. Designed with a modular architecture allowing hotend, extruder, and fan-duct modules to be swapped independently. Print-it-yourself.
Pros: True modular design — swap components without reprinting the whole head; flexible fan duct configurations
Cons: Community mod — verify current development status; source URL needs confirmation

Name: Rapid Burner
Description: Community toolhead for Voron 2.4 and Trident, inspired by Dragon Burner geometry but with optimized mass distribution for high-acceleration printing. Supports a wide range of hotends via the Dragon Burner-compatible mount system. Print-it-yourself.
Included Hotend: Dragon HF/UHF, Rapido HF, NF-Crazy, Revo Voron (Dragon Burner-compatible mounts)
Pros: Lower mass than StealthBurner; DB-compatible hotend mounts; good high-acceleration behavior
Cons: Less community support than Dragon Burner or Xol; source URL needs verification; designer attribution needs community confirmation

Name: RoundHouse
Description: A direct drive extruder designed for the Voron V0.1, built using BMG extruder kit guts and a NEMA14 36mm pancake motor. Uses the Mini-AfterSherpa mounting pattern and was designed to complement the 5015 Toolhead.
Pros:
BMG gear quality in a compact V0-compatible form factor
Mini-AfterSherpa mount pattern — wide toolhead compatibility
Well-documented by chirpy2605
Cons:
Work-in-progress — design may still change
Requires BMG kit + NEMA14 pancake motor sourcing
Needs printed parts

Name: RoundAbout
Description: A direct drive extruder for the Voron V0.1 that uses the guts of an Orbiter v2.0. Shares the Mini-AfterSherpa mounting pattern with the RoundHouse and was designed to complement the 5015 Toolhead.
Included Extruder: RoundAbout (this is the extruder — uses Orbiter v2.0 internals)
Pros:
Orbiter v2.0 internals in a V0-optimized housing
Mini-AfterSherpa mount — compatible with Mailbox and 5015 Toolhead
Lightweight design
Cons:
Work-in-progress status
Requires Orbiter v2.0 donor unit
Needs printed parts

Name: RoundTrip
Description: A Voron and Printers for Ants extruder series from chirpy2605 that uses either LGX Lite, TBG Lite, Orbiter v1.5, or Orbiter v2.0 extruder gears. Compatible with any printer using the Sherpa Mini mounting pattern.
Included Extruder: RoundTrip (extruder series — LGX Lite, TBG Lite, Orbiter v1.5, or Orbiter v2.0 gears)
Pros:
Supports four different extruder gear sets — highly flexible
Sherpa Mini mount pattern — broadest toolhead compatibility
Works on both V0 and full-size Vorons
Cons:
Requires sourcing your own extruder gears (LGX Lite, TBG Lite, or Orbiter internals)
Needs printed parts

Name: Yavoth
Description: A unibody toolhead for Voron printers optimized for high-flow and ultra-high-flow hotends. Features two 4010 part cooling fans angled front-to-rear and a 2510 hotend fan positioned higher in the cowl for improved cooling. Designed to stay within V0.2 MiniSB dimensions.
Included Hotend: High-flow and UHF hotends (Dragon, Rapido, Revo Voron, and UHF variants)
Pros:
Unibody design — rigid and easy to print with no supports needed
2510 fan positioned higher for better heatsink cooling
Angled 4010 fans improve airflow to nozzle
Stays within V0.2 MiniSB footprint
Compatible with Dragon Burner extras and Alternative Voron Mounts
Cons:
UHF variants lose 8.5mm Z height
No probe mounts integrated (use carriage-mounted probes)
May tap front door on some V0.2 installations

Name: Dragon Burner
Description: The Dragon Burner v8 is the community-standard lightweight toolhead for Voron V0.2 and Printers for Ants. CFD-tuned dual 4010 blower ducts, hotend cooling via a 3010 fan, and support for an enormous range of hotends and extruders. Mountable to all Voron printers via the Alternative Voron Mounts system.
Included Hotend: Most standard hotends (Dragon, Rapido HF, Revo Voron, V6, Volcano, and more — not UHF)
Included Extruder: Sherpa Mini, Orbiter v2, G2SA, LGX Lite, Wristwatch BMG/G2, Papilio Lite, and others
Pros:
CFD-optimized dual 4010 ducts — significant part cooling improvement over v7
Widest hotend and extruder compatibility of any V0 toolhead
Online configurator generates custom STL zip
Neopixel logo and nozzle LED support
Mounts for all Voron printers plus Tap and Boop
Cons:
V0.2 X-carriage only — V0.1 users must use Dragon Burner v4
Does not support UHF hotends (use Rapid Burner instead)

Name: AntHead
Description: Ultra-compact toolhead designed for the Voron V0 ecosystem and other micro-format CoreXY printers. Optimized for the tight constraints of V0 build volumes. Print-it-yourself design, maintained by the PrintersForAnts community mod collective.
Included Hotend: Mini-format hotends (Dragon Mini, Revo Micro, NF-Crazy)
Included Extruder: Mini Sherpa, Orbiter 1.5, LGX Lite (compact mounts)
Pros: Extremely compact; designed specifically for V0 constraints; active community from PrintersForAnts
Cons: Limited to micro-format printers; specific source URL needs verification; limited hotend options vs larger toolheads

Name: Rapid Burner
Description: The Rapid Burner v8 is the UHF-specific variant of the Dragon Burner for Voron V0.2 and Printers for Ants. Designed exclusively for Rapido UHF, Dragon UHF, Goliath Air, and Goliath Water hotends. Shares the same CFD-tuned v8 duct design as the Dragon Burner.
Included Hotend: Rapido UHF, Dragon UHF, Goliath Air, Goliath Water
Included Extruder: Sherpa Mini, Orbiter v2, G2SA, Wristwatch BMG/G2, and others
Pros:
Only toolhead in chirpy2605's lineup supporting Rapido UHF, Dragon UHF, Goliath Air, and Goliath Water
CFD-tuned v8 ducts
No X, Y, or Z travel loss
Neopixel LED support
Cons:
UHF and Goliath hotends only — not for standard or HF hotends
V0.2 X-carriage only (V0.1 use Rapid Burner v4)
Goliath nichrome wires require specific routing to avoid stress damage

Name: A4T
Description: Four-tool multi-material toolhead for Voron 2.4 and Trident. Designed for ERCF/Tradrack/similar MMU systems where a single toolhead handles 4 filament inputs. Maintains a compact form factor while supporting 4 independent filament paths. Compatible with the Xol mounting ecosystem.
Pros: 4-material capability without tool changer; compatible with Xol ecosystem; print-it-yourself cost; filament cutter included
Cons: Complex setup requiring MMU system; more bulk than single-material heads; less community support than Jabberwocky; source URL needs verification

Name: Mini-AfterSherpa
Description: A toolhead for the Voron V0.1 that adds support for standalone extruders using the Sherpa Mini mounting pattern. Bridges the gap between the Mini Afterburner's hotend mount ecosystem and the wide range of Sherpa Mini-compatible extruders.
Pros:
Enables standalone extruder support on V0.1 printers that otherwise require integrated extruder toolheads
Sherpa Mini mounting pattern — broad extruder compatibility
Created by PrintersForAnts community
Cons:
Older V0.1-focused design — V0.2 users should consider Dragon Burner
Limited part cooling compared to newer dual-fan designs

Name: StealthBurner
Description: Official Voron Design toolhead for Voron 2.4 and Trident. Successor to AfterBurner. Ships with Clockwork 2 (CW2) direct-drive extruder. Supports a wide range of hotends via official and community adapters. Two 5015 blower fans provide strong part cooling. Print-it-yourself design — no PCB required for basic wiring.
Included Hotend: Dragon HF, Dragon UHF, Revo Voron, Rapido HF, NF-Crazy (via adapters)
Pros: Official Voron toolhead — largest community support and mod ecosystem; strong part cooling; CW2 extruder is well-proven; many hotend adapters available
Cons: Bulkier than newer community designs; no filament cutter by default; not multi-material ready without mods; CW2 has more parts than some alternatives

Name: Dragon Burner
Description: Highly popular community toolhead for Voron 2.4, Trident, and V0. Known for supporting a very wide range of hotends including Dragon, Rapido, NF-Crazy, Revo, CHC Pro, Bambu X1C hotend, DropEffect, and more via the DB hotend mount system. Multiple versions (v6–v8). Dual 4010 fans on main version; separate V0 variant for compact printers.
Included Hotend: Dragon HF/UHF, Rapido HF/UHF, NF-Crazy, Revo Voron, CHC Pro, Bambu X1C hotend, DropEffect XG (and many others)
Included Extruder: Orbiter 2.0, LGX Lite, Sherpa Mini (via adapters)
Hotend Mount Style: Dragon Burner native mount system (many adapters)
Pros: Enormous hotend compatibility library; large community; well-documented; V0 variant available; Voron V0 Nozzle Cam mod support
Cons: GitHub repo appears archived/deleted as of mid-2026 — verify current source; 4010 fans may underperform 5015 on demanding overhangs

Name: Xol Toolhead
Description: Lightweight, compact print-it-yourself toolhead for Voron 2.4 and Trident. Designed to reduce inertia vs StealthBurner for high-acceleration printing. Supports a broad range of hotends and extruders via a modular hotend-mount system. Uses dual 4010 axial fans for part cooling. Compatible with Xol Carriage or stock Voron MGN12 carriage with adapter.
Included Hotend: Rapido HF/UHF, Dragon HF/UHF, DropEffect XG, NF-Crazy, Revo Voron, Chube Compact
Included Extruder: Sherpa Mini, G2SA, LGX Lite, Orbiter 2.0, DFA (via adapters)
Pros: Lower mass than StealthBurner — better for high-accel/IS tuning; modular hotend mounts support wide hotend range; active development; good community documentation
Cons: Dual 4010 fans provide less static pressure than 5015 blowers — may underperform on dense overhangs; less plug-and-play than CW2-based designs; no filament cutter native

Name: BreakNeck
Description: An experimental CoreXY toolhead for Voron printers focused on remote CPAP cooling and a deliberate post-extruder filament path bend to induce a bowden-like buffering effect. Designed by leddhedd and community-tested for several months. Now superseded by ARMPITHEIGHT.
Pros:
CPAP cooling provides more airflow than typical 5015 or 4010 fan setups
Experimental post-extruder filament path bend provides bowden-like buffering effect
Predecessor project to the more ambitious ARMPITHEIGHT ecosystem
Cons:
Superseded by ARMPITHEIGHT — active development has moved on
CPAP hose routing adds complexity
Experimental filament path not proven in production use

Name: Goliath A5T
Description: Five-tool multi-material toolhead from the VzBoT ecosystem. Designed for high-speed printing with 5-material switching capability. Intended for use with ERCF or similar MMU systems on VzBot and CoreXY platforms.
Pros: 5-material capability; VzBot ecosystem integration; print-it-yourself
Cons: Complex multi-material setup; primarily tuned for VzBot; source URL needs verification; limited community outside VzBot ecosystem

Name: FiberStream
Description: A community remix of the FibreStream toolhead by dr.rafi, published by Smolboi on Printables. Tested on Voron Trident with printed monolith gantry. The sheetmetal X carriage version provides minimal benefit on printed gantries per the designer's own testing.
Pros:
Remix of the FibreStream/dr.rafi toolhead design with improvements
Tested on Voron Trident with printed monolith gantry
Active development with community feedback
Cons:
Sheetmetal X carriage version offers little benefit on printed gantries
Ongoing project — parts may change
Limited documentation compared to established toolheads

Name: Mellow MultiHead Zero-Precision XYZ Nozzle Offset Calibration Tool (IDEX/INDX/StealthChanger)
Description: XYZ nozzle offset calibration tool for multi-tool systems (IDEX/INDX/StealthChanger). Vendor listing, not independently tested.

Name: Angry Tool Head
Description: A toolhead designed for the Monolith gantry system, targeting builders using the Voron ecosystem with a cross-gantry setup. Community-developed by Shamoon78.
Pros:
Specifically designed for Monolith gantry — fills a gap not covered by standard toolheads
Community-developed for advanced builders
Cons:
Monolith gantry required — not for standard CoreXY setups
Limited documentation and community testing data compared to established toolheads
Active development — design may change
